meetingObjectives: Show a credible FutureScaping-style monitoring product for Worthing using public evidence first.
Make the public evidence base useful immediately while clearly identifying client-controlled evidence layers.
Show how one proof area can expand into a fuller operational product when project datasets are supplied.

Scheme pages, overview plan sequence, public timing context, and candidate CCO profiles.

schemeNarrative.headline: A public-data-first shell for a repaired coastal-defence frontage
schemeNarrative.summary: The first release helps Worthing stakeholders understand scheme extent, available public evidence, and the client baseline layer needed for measured post-repair performance.
principles: Show the full scheme and one proof area clearly.
Keep provenance, dates, licence and CRS visible.
Use blue for gain/accretion and red for loss/erosion.
Treat profile-derived interpretation as contextual evidence until continuous surfaces are supplied.

timelineEvents.title: Capital maintenance repairs complete
timelineEvents.detail: Public sources say structural works completed in July 2026, establishing the public transition point into monitoring.

timelineEvents.title: July 2026 UAV baseline — client data required.
timelineEvents.detail: This project layer would convert the public-data view into measured post-repair monitoring once supplied.

timelineEvents.title: Possible shingle recycling window
timelineEvents.detail: Public materials indicate a future decision point if monitoring shows insufficient beach levels, but no threshold can be inferred from public sources.

timelineEvents.title: Second possible recycling window
timelineEvents.detail: This remains future planning context and should only become recommendation logic when agreed thresholds are supplied.

timelineContext.title: Repair-to-monitoring transition
timelineContext.detail: The review treats July 2026 as the public transition point from repair works into evidence-led monitoring, based on the council completion update dated 30 July 2026.

timelineContext.title: Public forcing context only
timelineContext.detail: Nearby waves, tides and weather can be shown to explain timing windows, but they must remain contextual until station quality and relevance are validated.

timelineContext.title: Future intervention windows stay non-binding
timelineContext.detail: Public references to later shingle recycling windows can support storyline planning, but not automated recommendations or threshold claims.

nonClaims: No measured post-repair surface change claim.
No implied one-to-one repair-performance link until asset alignment is verified.
clientAsk: July 2026 UAV baseline surface and metadata
Exact repaired groyne IDs and repair types
Design beach profile, crest or threshold values
Any permitted as-built or licence drawings needed for proof alignment
dataRules: Nearby wave and tide feeds are context only unless a Worthing-specific source is confirmed or configured.
Real-time and provisional records must be visually distinct from quality-controlled history.
Event context can explain timing pressure without implying engineering causation.
nextActions: Redraw public scheme geometry on a permitted baselayer for a live version.
Ingest and validate CCO profile series for the Pier East proof area.
Select timestamped elevation context layers with explicit date and licence metadata.
Attach source, date and quality metadata to every measured project layer.
